main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snowy roof slab (rows ~8-34) above a front wall with a wooden door, two lit windows with blue shutters and log base (rows ~36-62)
top_band: Pale white/light blue snow roof, rows ~8-34 (about 26 rows of light tones with shaded clumps), ending at a bright snow edge at rows ~32-34
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the roof is a big light snow surface (rows 8-33) that reads as a sloped top, then a bright snow-edge line at rows 32-34, followed by a dark eave shadow band at rows 36-39 with icicles, then the front wall (rows 40-62) with a plank door, windows set under shutters and log ends. The roof slope is clearly visible as a top surface above the front face, matching the reference houses, whose roofs are also seen as large slopes. The windows have shutters and a snow sill, giving some inset depth. There are no receding side faces.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 steps (white, pale blue-white, light blue-grey, mid blue-grey, shadow blue) in clumped patches, which reads as textured snow rather than flat fill. Wood uses several browns with plank grain and log ends. Outlines are dark brown beside wood and blue-grey beside snow, not black. The windows have a warm gradient with glow, and the shutters are shaded blue, with icicles, a chimney of stone, and bare branches adding detail. Tile density is high, comparable to the reference houses, and nothing reads as a sticker.
